rows.value: 25% main rate, 19% small profits rate, Marginal Relief between £50,000 and £250,000; 15% minimum effective rate for groups with revenue over €750 million. Paid by UK resident companies and UK permanent establishments of non-UK companies. Legal basis: Corporation Tax Acts 2009 and 2010; Finance (No.2) Act 2023 Parts 3 and 4. In force: financial year from 1 April 2026; top-up taxes for accounting periods beginning on or after 31 December 2023

source.title: HMRC: Corporation Tax rates and allowances (updated 1 April 2026)

rows.label: Branch profits and distributed profits [national]
rows.value: No separate branch profits tax: a UK permanent establishment pays Corporation Tax on the profits attributable to it. Paid by non-UK resident companies trading through a UK permanent establishment. Legal basis: Corporation Tax Act 2009 s. 5(2) and s. 19(1). In force: no start date stated

source.title: HMRC International Manual INTM262040: Non-residents trading in the UK: domestic charging provisions: Corporate Tax charge

rows.label: Self-employed contributions: Class 2 and Class 4 National Insurance [national]
rows.value: Class 4: 6% on profits between £12,570 and £50,270, 2% above; Class 2 treated as paid at profits of £7,105 or more, voluntary £3.65 a week below. Paid by self-employed people, through Self Assessment. Legal basis: Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 s. 15 (Class 4). In force: 2026-27 tax year, from 6 April 2026

source.title: HMRC National Insurance Manual NIM24001: Class 4 liability: general

rows.label: Contractor rules: off-payroll working (IR35) and the Construction Industry Scheme [national]
rows.value: IR35: the client decides status (the worker's own company for small private-sector clients) and the deemed employer deducts PAYE and National Insurance; CIS deductions 20% (registered), 30% (unregistered), 0% (gross payment status). Paid by clients, agencies and construction contractors (withheld from contractors' pay). Legal basis: ITEPA 2003 Part 2 Chapter 10 (IR35); Finance Act 2004 (CIS). In force: IR35 reform from 6 April 2021; CIS no start date stated

rows.value: Cash basis by default; £1,000 trading allowance; flat-rate expenses (£0.55 a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in 2026-27). Paid by sole traders and partnerships without corporate partners. Legal basis: Finance Act 2024 (cash basis default). In force: cash basis default from 6 April 2024; trading allowance from 6 April 2017

source.title: GOV.UK: Cash basis (printable guide)

rows.label: Non-resident tax on employment income (PAYE) [national]
rows.value: The normal Income Tax bands on UK employment income, withheld through PAYE; Personal Allowance for British and EEA citizens and others under a treaty. Paid by non-resident employees (employers withhold). Legal basis: Statutory Residence Test, Finance Act 2013 Schedule 45. In force: residence test from 6 April 2013

source.title: GOV.UK: Tax on your UK income if you live abroad (printable guide)

rows.label: Council Tax (domestic property tax) [local]
rows.value: Band D amount set by each council, other bands a fixed fraction of it; England average Band D £2,392 in 2026-27; Northern Ireland has domestic rates instead. Paid by occupiers aged 18 or over (owners of empty or second homes). Legal basis: Council Tax replaced the community charge on 1 April 1993; referendum limits under the Localism Act 2011. In force: 2026-27 financial year, from 1 April 2026

source.title: MHCLG: Council Tax levels set by local authorities in England 2026 to 2027: Technical Notes (published 25 March 2026)

rows.label: Business rates (non-domestic property tax) [local]
rows.value: England 2026-27: 43.2p to 50.8p per £1 of rateable value (retail, hospitality and leisure 38.2p and 43p); Scotland and Wales set their own multipliers. Paid by ratepayers of non-domestic property. Legal basis: Local Government Finance Act 1988 (Schedule 4ZA for the multipliers). In force: 2026-27 financial year, from 1 April 2026

source.title: GOV.UK: Estimate your business rates (multipliers for the 2026 to 2027 tax year)

rows.label: Stamp Duty Land Tax (England and Northern Ireland) [national]
rows.value: 0% to 12% on residential bands; +5% for additional dwellings; +2% for non-UK residents; 17% for certain companies over £500,000; non-residential 0% to 5%. Paid by buyers of land and property. Legal basis: Finance Act 2003. In force: residential rates from 1 April 2025

source.title: GOV.UK: Stamp Duty Land Tax (printable guide)

rows.label: Property transfer tax: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (Scotland) [devolved: Scotland]
rows.value: 0% to 12% on residential bands; first-time buyer nil band £175,000; Additional Dwelling Supplement 8% of the price; non-residential 0% to 5%. Paid by buyers of land and property in Scotland. Legal basis: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (Scotland) Act 2013. In force: residential rates from 1 April 2021; ADS rate from 5 December 2024

source.title: Revenue Scotland: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax: Residential property

rows.label: Property transfer tax: Land Transaction Tax (Wales) [devolved: Wales]
rows.value: 0% to 12% on main residential bands; higher residential rates 5% to 17%; non-residential 0% to 6%. Paid by buyers of land and property in Wales. Legal basis: Welsh legislation; rates set by Welsh Ministers and approved by the Welsh Parliament; collected by the Welsh Revenue Authority. In force: replaced SDLT in Wales from 1 April 2018; main rates from 10 October 2022

source.title: Welsh Revenue Authority: Land Transaction Tax rates and bands (last updated 10 December 2024)
